messages:
Alex B.: Heads up — we're validating the tenant-bridge proxy for the private deployment. Need clarity on RBAC delta for the new proxy SA and how it shows up in audit logs.
Maria G.: Quick Q — is this the sidecar proxy or a separate HA pair in the customer VPC?
Alex B.: Separate HA pair. Runs in a dedicated namespace on customer k8s. It terminates TLS to our control plane over mTLS, then rewrites headers and forwards to model-serving pods.
Samir P.: For RBAC I'd recommend granting the proxy service account only `get, list, watch` on Endpoints and Services + `create` on Events (for diagnostics). No Secrets read.
Jen L.: Agreed — Secrets must stay behind the keystore. How will the proxy authenticate to KMS to unwrap routing keys?
Alex B.: We plan to use instance-level HSM/KMS grant via the node IAM role. The proxy will call a local agent (kms-agent) with a short-lived token.
Maria G.: Do we have an audit trail for those unwrap ops? Customers need per-tenant key access logs.
Samir P.: KMS provider logs every Decrypt/Sign call. We also emit an internal audit-event when kms-agent returns a token. Those events go to local auditd and are forwarded to the collector with tenant_id, request_id, and SHA256(key_id).
Charlie (sec-bot): SECURITY: note that forwarding key_id hashes still counts as metadata — confirm customer acceptance for hashed identifiers.
Alex B.: @Charlie noted. We need to capture that in the design doc. Also want to test a simulated compromise: if proxy SA is compromised can it pivot to other namespaces? Need network policy proof.
Jen L.: Network policy: enforce `deny all` by default. Allow only from proxy HA namespace to model-serving namespace on the model port (grpc 5100). No kube API access. Proxy SA should not have rolebindings that allow pod exec.
Samir P.: We'll add a validating admission webhook that rejects any RoleBinding that includes the proxy SA outside its namespace. Also a periodic scan alert if cross-namespace bindings appear.
Maria G.: For e2e audit tests, can we script a small scenario: 1) valid request flow, 2) stolen SA token attempts to access kube-apiserver, 3) attempt to list secrets. Capture network captures + audit logs + KMS logs.
Alex B.: That's the plan. Draft of test plan snip: ```
# e2e test steps
1. create tenant namespace `t-foo`
2. deploy proxy HA set with SA `proxy-t-foo`
3. send signed request -> expect model response
4. inject token theft: use `kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:t-foo:proxy-t-foo get secrets`
5. assert can-i returns "no" and audit shows forbidden event
```
Samir P.: Also include a simulated egress gateway failure: ensure fallback policy doesn't send keys to an external telemetry endpoint.
Jen L.: Remediation playbook item: if audit shows proxy SA misuse, rotate node IAM role, disable proxy SA, and force KMS rotation for affected tenant. Add a runbook link.
Maria G.: Who owns the runbook and the validating webhook? Need owners to triage incidents.
Alex B.: Owner: Platform Security for webhook (Samir), DevOps for runbook (Jen). I'll add action items.
Charlie (sec-bot): ACTION CREATED: #SEC-1832 validating-webhook-hardening assigned to Samir P.
DevOps Bot: Deploy pipeline triggered for e2e test harness (job: proxy-e2e-audit) — build 202.
Samir P.: I'll spike the webhook this week and post a PR with test fixtures.
Jen L.: I'll author the runbook and include KMS log parsing queries and quick revocation commands.
Alex B.: Thanks. Let's keep the blast-radius small in the sim and capture all logs to a sealed bucket. Follow-up sync tomorrow 10am. :thumbsup:
